title: Level 4 (Expert) - C-8
notes:
West leads the ♠J against 3NT. West's lead is won by South. There are 8 top tricks (3 spades, 3 hearts, and 2 clubs). Dummy's heart suit is the most likely source of a ninth trick. Hearts are likely to divide 4-2 and South should try to guard against this possibility.

If South cashes the top hearts and that suit is indeed 4-2, the contract will be in trouble. By surrending a heart trick, the ninth trick can be developed, but South will be unable to reach his remaining spade winners. The defense will play clubs locking the lead in the dummy.

It would have done no good to cash the top spades before playing hearts. In this case, the defense would be in a position to cash enough tricks to defeat the contract upon winning the fourth round of hearts.

South can resolve his communication problems by ducking a heart at trick 2. By playing this way, South is able to establish a long heart trick while retaining a hand entry to cash the remaining spade honours. Dummy has 2 entries in clubs making it impossible for the defense to cut South off from the dummy.

It is true that South may go down by playing this way when hearts were 3-3 all along. The defense may be able to cash 4 diamond tricks after winning a heart trick. The recommended play is correct as the odds of hearts being 3-3 and diamonds being 4-1 are considerably less than the odds of a 4-2 heart break.
